text:
Architecture, agent interfaces and evaluation
A retail task walkthrough

An introduction to the tau2-bench repository and a concrete retail task. Technical details use commit 122e2432b82d740e8f313f46f0a071729c404f39. The walkthrough reconstructs source-code behavior, not a recorded model run. The repository has evolved beyond the original tau2 release. This deck focuses on the text-based interaction loop.

Sources:
https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench/blob/122e2432b82d740e8f313f46f0a071729c404f39/README.md
Conversational agents that use tools to complete customer-service tasks
A simulated customer reveals goals and responds to the agent.
Tool use in a stateful environment
Domain tools change orders and other records that evaluators inspect.
Domains include retail, airline and telecom. The repository also supports voice.

tau2-bench evaluates conversational customer-service agents in simulated domains with policies, tools, databases and user scenarios. The repository supports text half-duplex and voice full-duplex modes, as well as additional domains such as banking_knowledge and intake. This presentation uses the retail text loop to make the design concrete. A task reward measures the configured criteria rather than every possible property of real-world service quality.

Solid bidirectional arrows show runtime message exchanges. The orchestrator routes customer dialogue to the agent and sends tool calls to the environment. The tool environment holds mutable domain state. The orchestrator records the trajectory. The dashed arrow shows post-run evaluation, not an online decision maker. The evaluator also uses task criteria and fresh environments to reconstruct actual and reference states. The evaluation/replay diagram later makes those inputs explicit.

A clicky, full-size keyboard with RGB lighting.

If unavailable, accept no backlight.
A thermostat compatible with Google Home instead of Apple HomeKit.

Order #W2378156
Customer knows name and ZIP code, but has forgotten the email address.

Yusuf Rossi, ZIP 19122, wants a keyboard and thermostat exchange. The task asks the simulated customer to address everything in one go. The order is delivered. The customer requests Google Home compatibility, while the product data labels the target variant Google Assistant. This distinction is preserved in later slides.

The reference actions are not a mandatory script. They identify the user, read the order, read two products and request one combined exchange. Normal LLMAgent behavior does not use the reference solution as its prompt. Ground-truth/debug agents are a separate condition and must not be presented as an ordinary baseline. Task 0 has null natural-language assertions.

Example sequence: a customer asks about an order

Read downward in time. This illustrative cycle shows an order lookup, not a measured run. The agent may request further tools instead of replying after step 6, so the tool-use cycle can repeat. User and agent do not exchange messages directly. All arrows pass through the orchestrator. The environment changes state only for mutating calls; get_order_details is read-only. All messages and tool results enter the trajectory for later evaluation.

The preferred RGB keyboard exists, but it is unavailable
The agent should explain both replacements and obtain confirmation.

Keyboard old item 1151293680 maps to new item 7706410293. Thermostat old item 4983901480 maps to new item 7747408585. The clicky RGB full-size keyboard has available=false. The accepted fallback is clicky, no backlight, full-size. Arithmetic: 269.16 - 272.33 + 249.01 - 262.47 = -16.63. The negative difference records the exchange price difference, not completed bank settlement.

One request includes both items and their corresponding replacements

The tool checks order status, item membership, replacement availability
and the payment method before changing state.

This slide shows an abbreviated tool-call payload. Actual identifiers are strings, including item IDs. The function requires delivered status, checks item multiplicities and matching list lengths, resolves each new variant within the old product, checks availability and validates payment. A gift-card payment must cover a positive price difference. The function does not receive a user-confirmation token.

Sources:
https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench/blob/122e2432b82d740e8f313f46f0a071729c404f39/src/tau2/domains/retail/tools.py#L240

The environment records an exchange request
The write changes order fields rather than completing fulfillment
A second exchange call fails the delivered-status check.

The tool mutates the in-memory Order model in the retail environment. It records sorted item lists, payment method and the price difference. It does not replace order.items, ship products or settle a bank refund in this function. Since status becomes exchange requested, splitting the two exchanges into separate calls would cause the later call to fail the delivered-status requirement.

Sources:
https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench/blob/122e2432b82d740e8f313f46f0a071729c404f39/src/tau2/domains/retail/tools.py#L270
The evaluator reconstructs two states from the same starting point
Task 0: reward = DB × 1 for empty NL assertions, after normal termination.

The same evaluator coordinates both lanes. Both environments apply task initialization. Predicted state comes from the recorded trajectory; reference state comes from initial history plus reference actions. Current replay skips non-mutating and rejected calls and validates mutating tool outputs in strict mode. EnvironmentEvaluator compares agent and user database hashes. Other reward components depend on reward_basis. In base retail task 0, NL assertions are empty and contribute a neutral 1. Premature termination gives zero before this comparison.

A correct final state can hide a process violation
Hypothetical comparison: identical final states, different confirmation behavior
A policy requirement affects reward only when the task checks it.

This is a hypothetical source-based counterexample, not a measured result. Assume identical valid exchange calls and normal termination. The exchange tool lacks a confirmation credential argument, DB comparison cannot prove dialogue order, and base task 0 has no nonempty NL assertion. Other tasks can enable dialogue checks. The example shows why a benchmark result must be interpreted together with its active criteria.

The interface keeps the task environment independent of agent internals
External agents still need to follow a tool and message contract.

A normal text agent subclasses HalfDuplexAgent and implements get_init_state and generate_next_message. Inputs can include UserMessage, ToolMessage or MultiToolMessage. A registered factory supplies tools and domain policy. Registry changes must load in the runner process. Gym offers reset/step control, while the experimental agentify_tau_bench bridge exchanges A2A messages with a JSON action convention. These are integration options, not zero-adaptation support for every external agent. In-process tools do not provide a security sandbox.

Illustrative example: one task succeeds in 3 of 4 trials

pass^k = C(c, k) / C(n, k)
Compute per task, then average.

pass@k asks whether at least
one of k attempts succeeds.

This slide is a calculated illustration, not a benchmark result. n is the number of trials, c the number of successes, and k the number sampled without replacement. The implementation raises when n < k. pass^k measures repeated success while pass@k measures at least one success. A high score applies to the chosen task and simulator distribution and does not alone establish production readiness.

The framework is extensible, while each domain defines a narrower test
Tasks, users, agents and tools have separate interfaces.
DB, action and language checks cover only the criteria a task enables.
The shipped retail domain lacks coupon rules and delivery-date windows.

The framework provides extension points rather than a universal correctness definition. Retail models query, cancellation, modification and return/exchange requests. Its current order schema lacks delivery-date fields and its toolkit lacks a coupon or full checkout flow. Custom domains can add them. Standard Gym returns zero before completion and does not automatically supply dense per-step rewards. External side effects must be observable and replayable, or evaluated through another trustworthy state path.

Walkthrough: base retail task 0 at the pinned commit above.
Released benchmarks can use different task sets. Compare matched versions and settings.

The presentation is about tau2-bench only. Source-code paths cover the task schema, standard agent, orchestrator, retail tools, state replay and evaluators. The base retail collection has 114 tasks at the reviewed revision. Released text-v1 uses a frozen 50-task retail set with language-specific data binding, so this walkthrough must not be generalized to every released task. Pin code, data, agent configuration, user simulator and scoring configuration for comparable results.
